text:
anya: heads up — noticed a weird spike after today's runtime defaults deploy
matt: saw it too, routing weights moved for ~3% of requests
jordan: suspected deferred-default merge bug? details?
sasha: yeah — when default route is applied lazily the client merge can overwrite per-route cohorts
anya: exact flow: user sets route with blank 'preferred_backend', server sends default later -> client merges and writes back replacing weights
matt: ouch. so the console UI + client SDK doing a read-modify-write race
devex: can we avoid writeback from clients unless it's explicit? would break some workflows
jordan: proposal: server-side shallow-merge with etag check + reject if base changed. clients must send base_etag
sasha: +1. Also add a 'deferred_defaults_applied' telemetry flag so we can sample impacted requests
console-ui: UI change would be minor — show a banner when defaults are pending and disable auto-save
anya: quick code sample of incoming payload causing overwrite:
```json
{
  "route_id": "r-123",
  "weights": null,
  "preferred_backend": null
}
```
matt: clients currently transform null->{} and save. we should stop that
devex: ops-bot can we run a dry-run where server rejects blind merges and logs counts?
ops-bot: deploy-dryrun scheduled for 1789235600 — will emit `config.merge.rejected` events to telemetry
jordan: run cohort: 1% of traffic for 24h, check `config.merge.rejected` and latency/regressions
sasha: fallback plan: if merge rejected, return 409 + helpful payload telling client to re-fetch
anya: agreed. also add a console toggle to force server-side merge for specific orgs for emergency
matt: timeline: implement etag check + telemetry flag this week, dry-run tomorrow
devex: i'll draft console UX copy and add a canary toggle
console-ui: will add the banner + 'apply defaults now' button
anya: thanks team — please add playbook steps to the runbook if we see large `rejected` spikes
jordan: noted. posting followups in #incidents if we see anything
sasha: nice catch, anya :thumbsup:
